verses.text: Jesus left there and went to his home town, and his followers went with him.

When the Sabbath day came, he began to teach in the synagogue. Many people who heard him were amazed. "Where did this man get these things?" they asked. "What is this wisdom he has been given? How can he do such powerful miracles?
Is he not the carpenter, the son of Mary? Is he not the brother of James, Joses, Judas and Simon? Are his sisters not here with us?" And they would not accept him.
Jesus said to them, "A prophet is respected everywhere except in his own town, among his own relatives and in his own home."
He could not do any powerful miracles there. He only put his hands on a few sick people and healed them.
He was amazed that they had no faith. Then Jesus went around teaching from village to village.
He called the twelve to him and began to send them out two by two. He gave them authority over evil spirits.
He told them, "Take nothing for the journey except a walking stick. Take no bread, no bag and no money in your belts.
Wear sandals, but do not take an extra shirt."
He told them, "When you go into a house, stay there until you leave that town.

If any place will not welcome you or listen to you, shake the dust off your feet when you leave. This will be a warning to them. I tell you for certain, on the day of judgement it will be easier for Sodom and Gomorrah than for that town."
So they went out and preached that people should turn away from their sins.
They drove out many demons. They poured olive oil on many sick people and healed them.
King Herod heard about this, because Jesus' name had become well known. Some people were saying, "John the Baptist has been raised from the dead! That is why he has the power to do these miracles."
Others said, "He is Elijah." Still others said, "He is a prophet, like one of the prophets of long ago."
But when Herod heard this, he said, "It is John, the man I had beheaded. He has been raised from the dead!"
Herod himself had given orders to have John arrested. He had him tied up and put in prison. He did this because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip. Herod had married her.
John had been saying to Herod, "It is against the law for you to have your brother's wife."
So Herodias hated John and wanted to kill him. But she could not,
because Herod was afraid of John. He knew that John was a good and holy man, so he kept him safe. When Herod heard John speak, he was very troubled, but he still liked to listen to him.
Finally the right time came for Herodias. On Herod's birthday he gave a big dinner for his high officials, his army leaders and the most important men in Galilee.
The daughter of Herodias came in and danced. She pleased Herod and his dinner guests. The king said to the girl, "Ask me for anything you want, and I will give it to you."
He made a promise to her with an oath: "Anything you ask for I will give you, up to half of my kingdom."
She went out and said to her mother, "What should I ask for?" "The head of John the Baptist," her mother answered.
Straight away the girl hurried back to the king. She said, "I want you to give me the head of John the Baptist on a plate right now."
The king was very upset. But because of his oath and his dinner guests, he did not want to say no to her.
So straight away he sent a soldier with orders to bring John's head. The soldier went to the prison and cut off John's head.
He brought it back on a plate and gave it to the girl, and she gave it to her mother.
When John's followers heard about this, they came and took his body and put it in a tomb.
The apostles came back to Jesus. They told him all they had done and taught.
So many people were coming and going that they did not even have a chance to eat. So Jesus said to them, "Come with me by yourselves to a quiet place and get some rest."
So they went away by themselves in a boat to a quiet place.
But many people saw them leaving and recognised them. They ran there on foot from all the towns and got there ahead of them.
When Jesus got out of the boat, he saw a large crowd. He felt sorry for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd. So he began to teach them many things.
By that time it was late in the day. His followers came to him and said, "There is nothing here, and it is already very late.
Send the people away so that they can go to the nearby farms and villages and buy something to eat."
But Jesus answered, "You give them something to eat." They said to him, "That would take more than half a year's wages! Should we go and spend that much on bread and give it to them to eat?"
"How many loaves do you have?" Jesus asked. "Go and see." When they found out, they said, "Five, and two fish."
Then Jesus told them to make all the people sit down in groups on the green grass.
So they sat down in groups of a hundred and groups of fifty.

Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish. He looked up to heaven and gave thanks, and he broke the loaves. Then he gave them to his followers to hand out to the people. He also divided the two fish among them all.
They all ate and were satisfied.
The followers picked up twelve baskets full of pieces of bread and fish that were left over.
The number of men who had eaten was five thousand.
Straight away Jesus made his followers get into the boat and go on ahead of him to Bethsaida, while he sent the crowd away.
After saying goodbye to them, he went up on a mountain to pray.
When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the lake, and Jesus was alone on land.
He saw his followers working hard at rowing, because the wind was blowing against them. Shortly before dawn he went out to them, walking on the lake. He was about to pass by them.
But when they saw him walking on the lake, they thought he was a ghost, and they screamed.
They all saw him and were terrified. Straight away he spoke to them and said, "Be brave! It is I. Do not be afraid."
Then he climbed into the boat with them, and the wind stopped. They were completely amazed.
They had not understood what the loaves meant. Their hearts were still hard.
They crossed over the lake and landed at Gennesaret. There they tied up the boat.
As soon as they got out of the boat, the people recognised Jesus.
They ran through that whole area and began carrying sick people on mats to wherever they heard he was.

And wherever he went, into villages, towns or the countryside, they put the sick in the marketplaces. They begged him to let them touch just the edge of his clothes. And all who touched him were healed.
